strongest_valid_partial_result: The candidate proves that the Flint–Hills series converges if and only if the Diophantine sum sum 1/(n^3 ||n/pi||^2) converges, and gives a correct standard reduction to continued-fraction data.
fatal_gaps: Does not prove the lower bound |pi-p/q| >= q^{-nu} for all large q for every nu>2
Does not decide convergence of the Flint–Hills series
Key block estimate is only cited, not proved
evidence_quotes: We do not determine mu(pi), and we do not decide the convergence of the Flint–Hills series.
The exact value of mu(pi) is unknown.
Whether the Flint–Hills series converges is unknown.
notes: The manuscript explicitly refuses to prove the target theorem and instead presents partial reductions and open-problem discussion. Some of those reductions are correct and nontrivial as background, but the exact target statement mu(pi)=2 and its corollary are not established.
